## 🔒 Security Fixes

Flare 3.0.1 is a security release, so please update as soon as you can.

birb ([@parabirb](https://github.com/parabirb)) audited Flare 3.0 and sent me a detailed report with sixteen findings. I checked every one against 3.0.0 and fixed each one that held up, plus a few bugs that turned up while I was in there. Seven of them get an advisory:

| Severity | What could happen                                                                                                                                                 | Who's affected                                                                 | Advisory                                                                                        |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Critical | The repository's `docker-compose.yml` published PostgreSQL on every host interface with a password anyone could read, and shipped a placeholder `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` | Instances started from the repository's Compose file instead of the handbook's | [GHSA-m73c-m5qp-rw3g](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-m73c-m5qp-rw3g) |
| High     | An upload with a crafted name made a data export write files anywhere the app could, including over its own code                                                  | S3 storage                                                                     | [GHSA-g39q-crp4-2ch6](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-g39q-crp4-2ch6) |
| High     | An uploaded SVG's thumbnail URL could run script on your Flare origin with the visitor's session                                                                  | Instances where people you don't fully trust can upload                        | [GHSA-4fr7-p4rm-r2f6](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-4fr7-p4rm-r2f6) |
| High     | Classic appearance colors and the theme mode could put script on every page, including sign-in                                                                    | Instances that gave `appearance.manage` to someone who isn't an admin          | [GHSA-jf87-vxjh-6gv2](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-jf87-vxjh-6gv2) |
| High     | File passwords could be guessed with no limit, and a one-character password was allowed                                                                           | Password-protected files                                                       | [GHSA-qxr9-m5ff-27rv](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-qxr9-m5ff-27rv) |
| High     | Anyone could start unlimited OCR runs on a public image without saved text, and a failed run repeated on every request                                            | Any instance with public images                                                | [GHSA-7p5v-2m9m-3p9m](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-7p5v-2m9m-3p9m) |
| Medium   | Private and password-protected videos were sent as publicly cacheable for a year                                                                                  | Instances behind a CDN or caching proxy                                        | [GHSA-5gjg-xfq3-pp83](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/advisories/GHSA-5gjg-xfq3-pp83) |

There's also some hardening: every rate limit now reads the client address the same way (with a new `FLARE_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` for edges like Cloudflare), pages send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, the workflows pin every action to a commit, and you can now cap audit history with `FLARE_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`.

## 🐛 Fixes

- **Big uploads from API clients:** Next.js was cutting every API request body off at 10 MB, so direct uploads over 10 MB from ShareX, scripts, and other clients failed. They now work up to your configured limits.
- **Upload limits always hold:** an upload that ran into the size limit or your remaining quota early could be saved cut short and reported as a success. It's now refused with `413` and nothing is kept.
- **Names in other languages:** files up to 10 MB uploaded from the browser or with curl came out garbled when their names had accents or non-Latin scripts, like `cafÃ©.png`. New uploads keep their names. Files uploaded earlier keep the garbled name, but their links and contents are fine.
- **Rejected uploads answer right away** instead of hanging until the client gave up.
- **Cleaner URL names:** collision names and extensions are sanitized like everything else, and signed-out visitors can open public links whose names have no extension.
- **Data exports:** **Export All Data** now builds the ZIP while it downloads, keeps files that share a name as separate entries, stops when you leave the page, and no longer hangs on S3.
- **Byte ranges:** malformed or out-of-range requests get a proper `416` instead of an error, and suffix ranges return the right bytes on S3.
- **The classic color picker works:** it used to save hex values the theme couldn't read, which could leave a primary button transparent. Colors you picked earlier now show up as picked.
- **Less overhead per request:** view, download, and click counters no longer write a second audit event, and settings are parsed once per change instead of on every read.

## ❤️ Thanks

Huge thanks to birb for the audit. It came with working reproductions for the serious issues and a score for every finding, which made checking and fixing all of this a lot faster. If you find something, the [security policy](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/security/policy) explains how to report it privately.

## ⬆️ Updating

Back up your database and uploads, then update the image as usual. There are no database migrations, and nobody is signed out unless you change `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`. After updating:

- **If you started Flare with the repository's `docker-compose.yml`:** move to the new file before anything else. Set your own `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` and database password, and stop publishing PostgreSQL. The new file also publishes Flare on `127.0.0.1:3000` only, so reach it through your reverse proxy. If port 5432 was reachable from outside, treat that database and its credentials as exposed.
- **If a CDN or caching proxy sits in front of Flare:** purge everything cached under `/api/files/` once, with a prefix or wildcard purge rather than that single URL. That clears cached copies of protected videos and of thumbnails sent before the new policy.
- **If you use S3 storage and people you don't fully trust can upload:** search **Audit log** for `..` to find uploads whose names contain path segments. If you find any, rotate `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, your database password, and your S3 keys.
- **If you gave `appearance.manage` to anyone besides admins:** review appearance changes in **Audit log**. Unsafe saved colors are ignored and removed the next time settings are saved.
- **File passwords:** new ones need at least 8 characters. Existing passwords keep working until they're changed.

[Upgrade guide: 3.0 → 3.0.1](https://flintsh.github.io/Flare/versions/v3.0.1/hosting/maintenance.html#upgrading-from-3-0-to-3-0-1) · [Full changelog: v3.0.0 → v3.0.1](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/compare/v3.0.0...v3.0.1)

## 📦 Download & Deploy

AMD64 and ARM64 images:

```bash
# Docker Hub
docker pull docker.io/flintsh/flare:3.0.1

# GitHub Container Registry
docker pull ghcr.io/flintsh/flare:3.0.1
```
